===== NEW MESSAGES SINCE YOUR LAST TURN =====
**Codex (Design Lead · Skeptic) — Round 1**

I think the best direction is a staged MoSCoW map that locks a rules-complete, single-surface game slice now, with every deferred feature contractually listed for later. Anything else risks either a broken game engine or a fake “finished” look that this brief explicitly says is unacceptable.

Must: Foundation gameplay slice, draw-1 only, no placeholders
As-designed for this phase, everything must make this app truly playable and correct at launch.

MUST
- Correct Klondike rules engine (single deck, 7 tableau, 4 foundations, alternating-color descending tableau, King-on-empty, ascending same-suit foundation, no network/state leakage). This is the product’s anchor.
- One-screen game entry flow that opens to a restored board if present, or a fresh legal deal on first run/new game.
- Tap-to-move interaction model with three-state destination logic through one move core: single legal destination auto-executes; multiple legal destinations highlight and require confirm tap; zero destinations show blocked feedback.
- Tap-based run relocation as the run-capable rules behavior: moving the maximal face-up alternating sequence from tapped card as one unit.
- New Game/Deal resets only after explicit confirmation if current game is unfinished.
- Stock draw/recycle and waste behavior for draw-1, with deterministic logic and explicit unlimited redeal.
- Full multi-step undo with exact state restoration.
- Win and true stuck-board terminal detection as explicit end states, each surfaced clearly.
- Real atomic logical persistence (logical piles + face-up flags + timer state + undo stack + game seed/ordering), saved with temp-then-swap semantics; survives background/terminate/relaunch without corruption.
- “First paint” experience that is not a shell: real spring-based deal/flip sequence on fresh deal only (never replayed on cold-launch resume of an in-progress game).
- Local event capture from day one (session start/end, elapsed seconds, undo count, outcome), even though no Stats UI ships in this slice.
- In-app state honesty: no placeholders, no fake completion banners, no claimed times/trophies unless real.

Should
- Launch screen themed to app visual atmosphere instead of default white flash.
- Haptics on accepted/rejected move and win.
- Full accessibility for custom card UI (explicit VoiceOver labels, non-color-only suit cues, reduce-motion fallbacks for key animations).
- Theme-first styling with no hardcoded colors/fonts outside Theme tokens, with dark and light explicitly art-directed.
- Explicitly branded settings copy that explains local-only persistence behavior.
- Local stats/settings persistence architecture prepared for future settings/stats screens.

Could
- Add Settings and Stats tabs as peer surfaces via TabView once slice-1 build is stable.
- Expand to draw-3 in a separate increment with separate legality/persistence semantics.
- Live interactive drag (single and multi-card) after tap-and-move is proven stable.
- Win-screen image sharing (rendered board + solve caption) via native share sheet.
- Card-back theme pack, animation micro-polish (ambient parallax, shadow depth tuning), and gesture refinements.

Won’t-build
- Multiplayer, social feeds, leaderboards, Game Center, ads, IAP/subscription, analytics/telemetry, cloud sync/iCloud/CloudKit, or any backend.
- Seeded challenge/replay or encrypted shuffle logic.
- iPad-only restriction as a side effect of orientation locking.
- Any feature that alters correctness semantics for “completeness” claims in this phase.

In-scope for this phase: everything marked Must and the listed should items needed to test whether game correctness, persistence integrity, and launch motion feel pass the bar.
Out-of-scope for this phase: everything in Could until slice-1 is shippable and verified.

Must-have user stories and acceptance criteria
- As a player, I open the app and continue the exact game I left off. Acceptance: if a saved logical state exists, board restores without replaying deal animation; if none exists, game starts from valid fresh shuffle.
- As a player, I can make a legal move quickly with one tap. Acceptance: one legal destination auto-executes with spring transition and haptics; board mutation is persisted after completion.
- As a player with strategic choices, I can choose destination when more than one exists. Acceptance: legal targets render as highlighted destinations; second tap to confirm executes chosen move; no destination auto-chosen.
- As a player, I can move a legal tableau run in one action. Acceptance: tapping a run head identifies maximal valid face-up sequence and moves the whole sequence atomically to a legal destination.
- As a player, I can undo mistakes indefinitely within session depth. Acceptance: undo always returns to prior exact logical board state and timer/undo counters reflect restored game.
- As a player, I can always tell when the game is finished. Acceptance: win modal appears only when all 4 foundations complete; stuck modal appears only when no legal move exists under draw-1 static legality pass.
- As a player, I can restart without losing unsurfaced work by accident. Acceptance: New Game triggers confirmation whenever current state is not terminal.
- As a player, my data is safe to app lifecycle transitions. Acceptance: app background/kill/relaunch restores exact settled logical state; animation state is never serialized as source of truth.
- As a player, I get a real, immediate game feel. Acceptance: fresh deal always uses spring sequencing + card flip reveal with actual card art, no placeholder transitions.
- As a player, stats data is never invented. Acceptance: only recorded events from actual in-session data are persisted and used by future Stats implementation.

**Claude (QA & Risk · Pragmatist) — Round 1**

I want to flag the elephant in the room before I write a single feature line, because if we don't resolve it here, everything downstream inherits a contradiction: prompt_contract-011 defines "production-ready" as explicitly requiring zero placeholder screens among Game/Stats/Settings, and the original prompt itself asks for a Stats screen and a Settings screen with draw-1/draw-3 switching, card-back selection, and timer on/off. But next_steps_small and detailed_discussion spent three rounds each locking a "slice 1" that ships game-only — no TabView, no Settings UI, no Stats UI, draw-1 only, silent event recording with no surface to view it. Those were framed as "first increment," implying a second increment exists somewhere to finish the job. I don't see evidence anywhere in this pipeline that a second build increment is actually going to happen — there's no future build phase named for it. If this is genuinely a single build, "slice 1" isn't an increment, it's the whole app, and shipping it as scoped would fail this app's own locked production-readiness bar and the adherence gate that grades against the original prompt. I think this phase has to explicitly settle that, not quietly inherit the narrower scope by default.

My pragmatic read: build the full triad now — Game, Stats, Settings all real, all in a TabView, resume-first per DEC-initial_discussion-002 — but keep every correctness-critical decision from the slice-1 debates intact as the actual engineering approach inside Game (tap-to-move with the three-case model, run relocation, static draw-1 stuck-detection extended to also cover draw-3 legality, atomic persistence, no encryption, silent event logging feeding directly into the now-real Stats screen instead of sitting unused). The slice-1 arguments about *sequencing implementation risk* were good engineering discipline; they were never a good argument for *permanently cutting user-facing screens the prompt explicitly asked for*. Draw-3 has to actually work, not just exist as a Settings toggle with no real implementation behind it — a toggle that does nothing or silently misbehaves is worse than not offering it, and it's exactly the kind of "claims an outcome that didn't happen" failure this fleet has been burned by before.

On must-haves, here's where I'd draw the line, all traceable to already-locked decisions so nothing here is a new invention: the full Klondike rules engine (single deck, 7 tableau, 4 foundations, standard ascending/alternating rules); draw-1 and draw-3 both real and switchable via Settings gated behind new-game; tap-to-move with the single/multiple/zero-destination model plus run relocation; stock draw and unlimited redeal; full multi-step undo; explicit win and stuck-board terminal states; New Game confirmation over an unfinished board; the bespoke generative card-face system passing the native-size legibility gate — this is a hard pass/fail, not a nice-to-have, because an illegible glyph is a correctness bug, a player literally can't identify their own card; at least two card-back options selectable live; the real spring-based deal/flip animation gated to fresh deals only; both light and dark mode fully art-directed; haptics on move-accept/reject/win, verified by source inspection per DEC-prompt_contract-012; a real Stats screen with per-draw-mode games/wins/best-time/streak, showing N/A when timer is off; a real Settings screen with the three named controls plus the local-data-only disclosure line from [REDACTED:high_entropy]; timer semantics as locked (starts on first state-mutating action, pauses on background); logical-state-only persistence, atomic write, no encryption; VoiceOver labels and non-color-only suit cues; a themed LaunchScreen; portrait-only. That's a long list, but every item on it is already a decision in the log — I'm not adding scope, I'm refusing to let scope quietly evaporate between phases.

Should-haves: the win-screen share-image sheet from [REDACTED:high_entropy] (explicitly deferred once already, and I think that deferral was right — it's genuinely separable and lower-risk, unlike Stats/Settings which the prompt names as core deliverables); parallax/depth polish on cards beyond the base deal animation; extra ambient shadow tuning.

Could-haves: additional card-back designs beyond the minimum viable two or three; alternate haptic intensity.

Won't-build, all already locked and I see no reason to reopen: any variant beyond Klondike, multiplayer/social/leaderboards/Game Center, IAP/ads/subscriptions, accounts/analytics/telemetry, iCloud/CloudKit sync, live interactive drag (single or multi-card — [REDACTED:high_entropy] was explicit that run-relocation via tap is in scope but the live gesture stays out), landscape/iPad-specific layout investment, Keychain/encrypted storage, seeded-challenge replay sharing.

The thing I most want preserved in the final output isn't the list itself, it's the acceptance-criteria discipline behind it: every must-have needs a criterion that's actually falsifiable by inspection or a scripted test, not "feels good" — e.g. for stuck-board detection, "given a board with zero legal moves across tableau/foundation/waste-top for the active draw mode, the app surfaces the stuck-state UI within one frame of the last move, and this is verified with at least one hand-constructed stuck board per draw mode, not just organically encountered." If the requirements-json isn't that concrete, the adherence gate that reads it directly will end up grading against vibes, and given this app's history of near-misses on exactly this kind of ambiguity, that's the failure mode I'd bet on if we don't nail it down now.

**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 1**

Both of them built out full MoSCoW lists, and there's real overlap on the mechanics — but they're actually arguing about something bigger than either list admits, and I don't want to paper over it.

**Where they agree:** the core rules engine (single deck, 7 tableau, 4 foundations, standard Klondike legality), the three-case tap-to-move model plus tap-based run relocation, full multi-step undo, explicit win/stuck-board detection, atomic no-encryption logical-state persistence, silent event logging from day one, deal/flip gated to fresh deals only, New Game confirmation, portrait lock, no live drag/multiplayer/IAP/accounts/cloud sync — all of this is just restating decisions the pipeline already locked in earlier phases, and neither agent is contesting any of it.

**Where they actually diverge, and it's a real fork:** Codex scoped this phase's must-haves to the "slice 1" game-only build that next_steps_small and detailed_discussion spent six rounds negotiating — Settings, Stats, and draw-3 all pushed to "could-have," i.e., a later increment. Claude is challenging the premise underneath that framing directly: those six rounds all talked about "slice 1" as if a second build increment obviously follows it, but nothing in this pipeline actually names a second build phase — app_features feeds into design/build phases for one production-ready app, not a phase-2 build. If that's right, "slice 1" isn't an increment, it's the whole deliverable, and shipping it without real Stats/Settings screens would directly violate DEC-prompt_contract-011's "zero placeholder screens among Game/Stats/Settings" bar and would fail this app against its own original prompt, which explicitly asks for both screens plus draw-1/draw-3 switching. Claude's position: build the full triad (Game/Stats/Settings, TabView, resume-first) now, with draw-3 as a real, fully-working mode (not a toggle that silently misbehaves), while keeping every slice-1 correctness discipline intact as the engineering approach.

This is the actual question the next round needs to answer before either MoSCoW list can be finalized: **is there a build phase after this one, or is this the only build this app gets?** Everything else is downstream of that.

CONSENSUS: NO

## What's still open

Round 2 needs to settle: (1) whether Settings/Stats screens and draw-3 are must-haves for this phase's requirements list (Claude's position) or legitimately deferred could-haves because a real second increment exists (Codex's position) — and that needs to be checked against the actual phase pipeline, not assumed; (2) if the full triad ships now, whether draw-3 gets its own stuck-detection design (per [REDACTED:high_entropy]'s explicit carve-out that the static draw-1 shortcut doesn't transfer) or whether that's too much new algorithmic surface for this build; (3) concrete, falsifiable acceptance criteria per must-have, which Claude flagged as necessary since the adherence gate reads the requirements-json directly.

[REDACTED:high_entropy] was right to say the draw-1 static-pass shortcut doesn't transfer, and here's concretely why: in draw-1, every card sitting in stock or waste is guaranteed to eventually surface as the waste top on its own, one at a time, so "treat every stock+waste card as a hypothetical waste-top" is exact. In draw-3, cards surface in groups of three and only the front of each group is playable until you draw past it, and which cards end up grouped together shifts every time the pile reshuffles back from waste to stock — so proving exact reachability is a real combinatorial problem I don't think we should try to solve precisely under this build's time budget. My pragmatic fix: reuse the same permissive static pass for draw-3 too — treat every card currently in stock or waste as a hypothetical candidate, exactly like draw-1 — but document explicitly that this is a conservative approximation, not an exact proof, and design it to fail toward "don't declare stuck" rather than "falsely declare stuck." That's the right direction to be wrong in: a board that's actually stuck but doesn't show the stuck modal yet is mildly annoying, the player just keeps drawing and finds out; a board that falsely tells the player "you're stuck, game over" when a real move existed is a much worse trust violation, on an app whose entire pitch is "we don't lie to you about your own data." I'd rather ship a slightly conservative stuck-check than an exact one we don't have time to prove correct.

Last thing, since I promised concrete acceptance criteria and mostly gestured at the idea last round instead of writing them: the Stats screen needs an explicit empty state before any game exists for that mode, and that's not optional polish — it's the global "every screen needs empty/loading/success/error" rule colliding directly with the "N/A best time" and "no fabricated data" rules we've already locked. Acceptance criteria should read something like: on first launch, before any game is completed in a given draw mode, that mode's stats show a real empty state ("0 games played" or equivalent), never a placeholder number, never the other mode's numbers, and never blank. And for the draw-mode setting specifically: selecting draw-3 while a draw-1 game is mid-progress must trigger the same confirmation pattern already locked for New Game — if the player confirms, the current game is discarded and a fresh draw-3 deal starts; if they cancel, the setting value doesn't change and the in-progress game is untouched. That's the kind of criterion that's actually testable by someone poking at the app, not just prose we hope gets implemented faithfully.
